thesis: Hold. The one decision-relevant new item today is that the August CPI report lands this session, and that argues for doing nothing rather than something. I have spent the last three sessions building a position for exactly this macro question: I cut NVDA on the U.S.-Iran escalation, opened XOM on crude approaching 100 dollars with a named inflation channel, and added a small amount on the IEA's confirmation of the Hormuz blockade. The book now carries roughly 13% energy against roughly 80% long-duration tech, which is my inflation view expressed at a size I chose deliberately. CPI will either support that view or undercut it, and I have no idea which. Adding to the energy tilt this morning would be betting on the print, and trimming tech this morning would be betting on it in the other direction; both are wagers on a number I cannot know before the open, which is precisely the kind of trade the no-lookahead rule exists to prevent. The honest move is to let the positioning I built on evidence face the event as it stands. The accompanying detail that stock futures are rising ahead of the report changes nothing, for the reason I have given every time futures appear in a pack: they move before the open, I fill at the open, and that information is already in my execution price. Nothing else in the pack reaches my universe. The unnamed 'energy stock insider doubles down' item does not identify a ticker in its headline, and I will not guess at which company it means in order to manufacture a trade. Morgan Stanley's upgrade of Synopsys is an analyst action on a name I cannot trade, the Google and Microsoft veteran's remarks on AGI hype are opinion, and HIVE, Beam, AT&T, Principal's new ETF and the AFRC audit fine are all outside the 20 symbols. Everything else is carried over from the last two packs and already adjudicated. Mechanically I also have little room to act even if I wanted to: cash is about 7% of equity against my 5% floor, so any meaningful buy would now require selling tech into a CPI morning. The book stands at 4 of 8 positions with NVDA near 39%, well inside the 50% cap.
